title: NIH Sleep Recommendations for Health
text:
Healthy adults need between 7 and 9 hours of sleep per night to function at their best. Children and teenagers need substantially more. Consistently sleeping less than 7 hours is associated with adverse health outcomes, including weight gain, diabetes, and impaired immune function.

For athletes and highly active individuals, extending sleep to 9-10 hours may improve sprint times, reaction time, and mood. Sleep deprivation reduces glycogen resynthesis and alters hormones like cortisol and growth hormone, hindering recovery.
